invocation-delay.description: Adds a configurable delay to Lambda function invocations to evaluate application behavior and resilience under increased execution latency.
invocation-delay.impact: Requests invoking the function may experience increased latency, timeouts, downstream delays, or cascading failures depending on the configured delay.
invocation-delay.expected_behavior: The application should tolerate the added latency within defined thresholds, maintain acceptable error rates, and recover normally when the experiment ends.

invocation-error.description: Injects errors into Lambda function invocations to evaluate how the application handles function execution failures.
invocation-error.impact: Lambda invocations may fail and dependent applications may receive errors, potentially triggering retries or fallback behavior.
invocation-error.expected_behavior: The application should detect invocation failures, handle them gracefully, and recover automatically after the fault is removed.

http-response.description: Injects configurable HTTP responses from Lambda integrations to test application behavior when downstream responses contain controlled error or status conditions.
http-response.impact: Applications consuming the Lambda HTTP integration may receive unexpected HTTP status codes and may trigger error handling, retries, or fallback paths.
http-response.expected_behavior: The application should correctly interpret the injected response, execute its error-handling path, and recover after the experiment completes.

pause-global-table-replication.description: Pauses replication for an Amazon DynamoDB global table to evaluate application resilience during cross-Region replication interruptions.
pause-global-table-replication.impact: Changes made in one Region may not immediately replicate to other Regions, potentially causing temporary data divergence or stale reads.
pause-global-table-replication.expected_behavior: The application should tolerate temporary replication lag, continue operating within acceptable consistency requirements, and converge after replication resumes.

reboot-instance.description: Reboots an Amazon RDS database instance to evaluate application resilience during a database restart.
reboot-instance.impact: Database connections may be interrupted and applications may experience temporary connection failures, query errors, or increased latency.
reboot-instance.expected_behavior: Applications should detect the temporary database interruption, reconnect automatically, and resume normal operation after the instance becomes available.

failover-db-cluster.description: Triggers an Amazon RDS database cluster failover to test application resilience during a database role transition.
failover-db-cluster.impact: Active database connections may be terminated and applications may temporarily experience connection failures or increased latency during failover.
failover-db-cluster.expected_behavior: Applications should reconnect to the new database writer, tolerate transient errors, and return to normal operation without manual intervention.

interrupt-az-power.description: Simulates an Availability Zone power interruption for an Amazon ElastiCache replication group to evaluate cache resilience and multi-AZ recovery.
interrupt-az-power.impact: Cache nodes in the affected Availability Zone may become unavailable, causing cache misses, increased application latency, or temporary connection failures.
interrupt-az-power.expected_behavior: The application should continue operating using surviving cache nodes or fallback mechanisms and recover as the ElastiCache service restores capacity.

stop-instances.description: Stops selected Amazon EC2 instances to evaluate application resilience during instance interruption.
stop-instances.impact: The selected instances become unavailable and applications may experience connection failures, reduced capacity, or service disruption if sufficient replacement capacity is not available.
stop-instances.expected_behavior: Applications should tolerate the instance interruption, maintain availability through redundancy or recovery mechanisms, and return to normal operation when the instances are started again.

reboot-instances.description: Reboots selected Amazon EC2 instances to evaluate application resilience during an instance restart.
reboot-instances.impact: The selected instances temporarily become unavailable, which may interrupt running workloads, connections, or application requests.
reboot-instances.expected_behavior: Applications should tolerate the temporary interruption, reconnect automatically where applicable, and recover normally after the instances become available.

terminate-instances.description: Terminates selected Amazon EC2 instances to evaluate application resilience to permanent instance loss.
terminate-instances.impact: The selected instances are permanently terminated and workloads running on them may be disrupted or lost unless protected by redundancy, autoscaling, or recovery mechanisms.
terminate-instances.expected_behavior: The application should remain available through redundant capacity, autoscaling, or workload recovery mechanisms and restore the required capacity automatically.

spot-instance-interruption.description: Simulates an Amazon EC2 Spot Instance interruption to evaluate workload resilience against unexpected capacity reclamation.
spot-instance-interruption.impact: The affected Spot Instance may be interrupted and workloads running on it may experience termination, connection loss, or temporary capacity reduction.
spot-instance-interruption.expected_behavior: Applications should handle Spot interruptions gracefully through checkpointing, workload redistribution, retries, or replacement capacity.

insufficient-instance-capacity-error.description: Simulates an EC2 insufficient instance capacity error to evaluate application and infrastructure behavior when the requested capacity cannot be provisioned.
insufficient-instance-capacity-error.impact: New instance provisioning may fail, potentially reducing available application capacity or preventing recovery and scaling operations.
insufficient-instance-capacity-error.expected_behavior: Infrastructure and applications should handle capacity provisioning failures gracefully through retries, alternative capacity, scaling strategies, or other recovery mechanisms.

asg-insufficient-instance-capacity-error.description: Simulates insufficient EC2 capacity during Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling operations to evaluate resilience when replacement instances cannot be launched.
asg-insufficient-instance-capacity-error.impact: An Auto Scaling group may be unable to launch replacement instances, potentially reducing available capacity and affecting application availability.
asg-insufficient-instance-capacity-error.expected_behavior: The Auto Scaling configuration should handle provisioning failures through retry, alternative capacity, or other configured recovery mechanisms while maintaining acceptable service availability.

ebs-pause-volume-io.description: Pauses I/O operations on selected Amazon EBS volumes to evaluate application resilience to temporary storage unavailability.
ebs-pause-volume-io.impact: Applications using the affected volumes may experience blocked or failed I/O operations, increased latency, or application errors.
ebs-pause-volume-io.expected_behavior: Applications should tolerate temporary storage I/O disruption and recover correctly when volume I/O is restored.

ebs-volume-io-latency.description: Introduces configurable latency into read and write operations on selected Amazon EBS volumes to evaluate application behavior under degraded storage performance.
ebs-volume-io-latency.impact: Storage operations may become slower, increasing application latency, reducing throughput, and potentially causing timeouts under sustained I/O pressure.
ebs-volume-io-latency.expected_behavior: Applications should tolerate increased storage latency within defined thresholds and recover normal performance after the experiment ends.

kinesis-provisioned-throughput-exception.description: Injects ProvisionedThroughputExceededException errors into requests made to selected Kinesis Data Streams.
kinesis-provisioned-throughput-exception.potential_impact: Applications may experience failed read or write requests, increased retries, processing delays, or temporary disruption to data ingestion and consumption.
kinesis-provisioned-throughput-exception.expected_behavior: Applications should handle throttled requests through appropriate retry and exponential backoff mechanisms while maintaining stable stream processing.

kinesis-expired-iterator-exception.description: Injects ExpiredIteratorException errors into GetRecords requests for selected Kinesis Data Streams.
kinesis-expired-iterator-exception.potential_impact: Stream consumers may fail to retrieve records, resulting in processing delays, retries, or temporary interruption of shard consumption.
kinesis-expired-iterator-exception.expected_behavior: Consumers should detect expired iterators, obtain a new shard iterator, and resume record processing successfully.

kinesis-api-internal-error.description: Injects internal API errors into selected Kinesis operations made by the targeted IAM role.
kinesis-api-internal-error.potential_impact: Kinesis API requests may temporarily fail, causing read or write errors and potentially interrupting stream processing.
kinesis-api-internal-error.expected_behavior: Applications should handle transient API failures using error handling, retries, exponential backoff, and appropriate monitoring.

kinesis-api-throttle-error.description: Injects throttling errors into selected Kinesis API operations made by the targeted IAM role.
kinesis-api-throttle-error.potential_impact: Kinesis requests may be throttled, resulting in failed API calls, increased latency, retries, and reduced application throughput.
kinesis-api-throttle-error.expected_behavior: Applications should respond to throttling with exponential backoff and retry mechanisms while maintaining acceptable processing performance.

kinesis-api-unavailable-error.description: Injects service-unavailable errors into selected Kinesis API operations made by the targeted IAM role.
kinesis-api-unavailable-error.potential_impact: Kinesis API requests may temporarily fail, potentially interrupting data ingestion or consumption.
kinesis-api-unavailable-error.expected_behavior: Applications should tolerate temporary service unavailability through retries, backoff, fault handling, and recovery mechanisms.

stop-task.description: Stops a running Amazon ECS task to evaluate service resilience and task replacement behavior.
stop-task.impact: The selected task becomes unavailable and requests may be affected if the service does not have sufficient healthy replacement capacity.
stop-task.expected_behavior: ECS should replace the stopped task when configured to maintain desired capacity, while the application continues serving traffic with minimal disruption.

cpu-stress.description: Generates CPU stress inside an ECS task to evaluate application behavior under sustained CPU resource pressure.
cpu-stress.impact: CPU utilization may increase significantly, potentially causing higher latency, reduced throughput, task health degradation, or request failures.
cpu-stress.expected_behavior: The service should remain within acceptable performance thresholds and ECS should maintain healthy task capacity through scaling or replacement mechanisms.

io-stress.description: Generates I/O stress inside an ECS task to evaluate application resilience when storage or I/O resources are under pressure.
io-stress.impact: I/O latency and resource utilization may increase, potentially slowing application operations and affecting request performance.
io-stress.expected_behavior: The application should tolerate increased I/O latency and continue operating within defined performance and availability thresholds.

network-latency.description: Introduces network latency for an ECS task to evaluate application behavior under degraded network communication conditions.
network-latency.impact: Communication with dependent services may become slower, causing increased request latency, timeouts, retries, or reduced throughput.
network-latency.expected_behavior: The application should tolerate network delays through appropriate timeouts, retries, circuit breakers, or fallback mechanisms.

packet-loss.description: Injects network packet loss into an ECS task to evaluate resilience against unreliable network communication.
packet-loss.impact: Requests between the task and dependent services may fail or require retransmission, resulting in increased latency and transient errors.
packet-loss.expected_behavior: The application should handle transient network failures gracefully and recover when normal network conditions return.

zonal-autoshift.description: Tests Availability Zone traffic shifting behavior for Elastic Load Balancing to evaluate application resilience during zonal impairment.
zonal-autoshift.impact: Traffic may be shifted away from an affected Availability Zone, temporarily changing traffic distribution across healthy zones.
zonal-autoshift.expected_behavior: Healthy targets should continue serving traffic and the application should remain available while traffic is redistributed.

inject-kubernetes-custom-resource.description: Injects a Kubernetes custom resource into an Amazon EKS cluster to evaluate how workloads and controllers respond to controlled cluster changes.
inject-kubernetes-custom-resource.impact: The injected resource may trigger Kubernetes controllers or application behavior depending on the resource definition.
inject-kubernetes-custom-resource.expected_behavior: The cluster and applications should handle the injected resource safely without unexpected service degradation.

pod-cpu-stress.description: Generates CPU stress inside an EKS pod to evaluate workload behavior under CPU resource pressure.
pod-cpu-stress.impact: The affected pod may experience increased CPU utilization, higher latency, reduced throughput, or health degradation.
pod-cpu-stress.expected_behavior: Kubernetes should maintain workload availability through resource controls, scheduling, autoscaling, or pod replacement where configured.

pod-delete.description: Deletes a selected Kubernetes pod to test workload recovery and Kubernetes controller behavior.
pod-delete.impact: The selected pod becomes unavailable and requests may be affected while a replacement pod is created and becomes ready.
pod-delete.expected_behavior: The owning Kubernetes controller should recreate the pod and the application should return to healthy operation automatically.

pod-io-stress.description: Generates I/O stress inside an EKS pod to evaluate application resilience under storage and I/O pressure.
pod-io-stress.impact: The pod may experience increased I/O latency, slower processing, or degraded application performance.
pod-io-stress.expected_behavior: The workload should remain within acceptable performance limits and recover after the injected stress is removed.

pod-memory-stress.description: Generates memory stress inside an EKS pod to evaluate workload behavior under memory pressure.
pod-memory-stress.impact: The pod may experience increased memory utilization, degraded performance, or an out-of-memory termination if limits are exceeded.
pod-memory-stress.expected_behavior: Kubernetes should maintain service availability through appropriate resource limits, restarts, scheduling, and scaling mechanisms.

pod-network-blackhole-port.description: Blocks network communication to a selected port for an EKS pod to evaluate resilience against unavailable network endpoints.
pod-network-blackhole-port.impact: Connections to the affected port may fail or time out, potentially disrupting communication with dependent services.
pod-network-blackhole-port.expected_behavior: The application should detect the unavailable endpoint and use retries, failover, or other recovery mechanisms where configured.

pod-network-latency.description: Introduces network latency for an EKS pod to evaluate application resilience under degraded network conditions.
pod-network-latency.impact: Communication with other services may experience increased latency, timeouts, retries, and reduced throughput.
pod-network-latency.expected_behavior: The application should tolerate the additional latency and recover normally when network conditions return to normal.

pod-network-packet-loss.description: Injects packet loss into an EKS pod's network traffic to evaluate resilience against unreliable network communication.
pod-network-packet-loss.impact: Network requests may fail or require retransmission, resulting in increased latency and transient application errors.
pod-network-packet-loss.expected_behavior: The application should handle transient network failures gracefully and recover once packet loss is removed.

terminate-nodegroup-instances.description: Terminates instances belonging to an EKS managed node group to evaluate cluster and workload resilience during node loss.
terminate-nodegroup-instances.impact: Pods running on terminated nodes may be disrupted and require rescheduling onto remaining or newly provisioned nodes.
terminate-nodegroup-instances.expected_behavior: Kubernetes should reschedule affected workloads and the node group should restore capacity according to its configured scaling and recovery behavior.

pause-replication.description: Pauses Amazon S3 bucket replication to evaluate application behavior during temporary cross-Region or destination replication interruption.
pause-replication.impact: Objects written to the source bucket may not immediately appear in the destination bucket, creating temporary replication lag.
pause-replication.expected_behavior: Applications should tolerate temporary replication delays and continue operating according to their configured consistency and recovery requirements.
